verdict.rationale: LaunchDarkly has a first-party doc page on decision making with Bayesian statistics for its experimentation product. That page describes how results identify a winning or leading variation, so there is a documented statistics engine behind experiment results. However, the evidence is thin, consisting of a page title plus one sentence. Nothing documents variance-reduction options or a frequentist alternative, both of which the story names. Missing for 10: variance-reduction options (e.g. CUPED), any frequentist mode, in-depth methodology documentation, independent or hands-on corroboration of result trustworthiness.

support.subject: As a product manager, I can trust a documented statistics engine (Bayesian or frequentist, with variance-reduction options) behind experiment results

citations.quote: LaunchDarkly highlights the leading variation when there is not yet enough experiment data to declare a winning variation.
